source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.

injury: transverse amputations, anterior and posterior wounds, post-pharyngeal level

intervention.description: Post-pharyngeal fragments with two transverse wounds placed in 127 uM octanol right after cutting.

readout.method: macroscopic scoring of anterior-posterior pattern of regenerates

notes: Text gives only an approximate maximum ("~100%") at the post-pharyngeal area; exact value and n are in the Figure 1A chart (not on disk). Values for other amputation levels are chart-only. Duration 3 days taken from Figure 5 legend / Discussion; timepoint from Figure 1C legend.

source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.

stage: head-containing fragments (original head retained, posterior wound only)
injury: transverse amputation at varying levels along the A/P axis, posterior-facing wound only

intervention.description: Fragments retaining the original head, cut transversely at various A/P levels, placed in 127 uM octanol right after cutting.

readout.method: macroscopic scoring of anterior-posterior pattern of regenerates

notes: Paper gives only a bound: ">95% single-head (normal)" pooled over cut levels; entered as 95/5. Remainder assigned to double_head because legend says these fragments gave "very few" two-headed regenerates. n not stated; exact values chart-only.

source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.

injury: transverse amputations producing 5 fragments along the A/P axis; pharyngeal fragment

intervention.target: Dj-Inx-5, Dj-Inx-13, Dj-Inx-12 (innexin gap junction proteins)
intervention.timing: amputation ~25-28 days after first dsRNA injection
intervention.description: Worms injected with Dj-Inx-5 + Dj-Inx-13 dsRNA (3 consecutive days) then Dj-Inx-12 dsRNA (2 days, two weeks later), then cut into 5 fragments; pharyngeal fragment scored.

readout.method: macroscopic scoring of anterior-posterior pattern of regenerates

notes: Paper: 20%, n=21 (inverted A/P axis and two heads); 20% of 21 = 4.2, rounded to 4. Remainder assumed normal (paper does not describe the other animals). timing_start_h uses 25 days (stated ~25-28 days). TYPE NOTE: INSTRUCTIONS.md says innexin RNAi = gap_junction_knockdown, but harness/validate_rows.py rejects that type; stored as gap_junction_block with action knockdown so the validator passes.

source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.

intervention.target: Dj-Inx-5, Dj-Inx-13, Dj-Inx-12 (innexin gap junction proteins)
intervention.timing: dsRNA injections into intact worms; no amputation
intervention.description: Intact worms injected with Dj-Inx-5 + Dj-Inx-13 dsRNA (3 consecutive days) then Dj-Inx-12 dsRNA (2 days, two weeks later); no cutting.

notes: "other" = intact animals developing extra photoreceptor-like pigmentation and extra pharynxes (new axes in post-pharyngeal region) without amputation: ~50%, n=30. Remainder entered as normal anatomy although not described. Same group also reported: behavioural changes ~95% (n=137), fissioning ~43% (n=137), mortality ~37% (not entered as dead_count because denominator differs). TYPE NOTE: INSTRUCTIONS.md says innexin RNAi = gap_junction_knockdown, but harness/validate_rows.py rejects that type; stored as gap_junction_block with action knockdown so the validator passes.

source.title: Long-range neural and gap junction protein-mediated cues control polarity during planarian regeneration.

injury: transverse amputations plus lateral cuts interrupting the ventral nerve cords

intervention.target: gap junctions (innexins); ventral nerve cord continuity
intervention.description: Post-pharyngeal fragments given additional lateral cuts through the ventral nerve cords and placed in 127 uM octanol.

readout.method: macroscopic scoring of anterior-posterior pattern of regenerates

notes: "other" = all 38: ~20% (7.6, rounded to 8) formed anterior structures in all four blastemas (four heads); the remaining ~30 formed two or three heads (split not given in text; legend says all treated animals had A/P polarity changes). Two-headed animals could not be separated from three-headed ones, so none were placed in double_head. Exact distribution is in the Figure 4A chart (not on disk).
